source_text: {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὕτω φημὶ καὶ αὐτός· οὕτω γὰρ ἔφασκεν ὁ Χριστὸς, ὅτι «Ὧ πολὺ παρέθεντο, πολὺ ζητήσουσι παρ' αὐτοῦ·» Δῆλον δὲ ὅτι καὶ τὸ ἔμπαλιν ἀληθές· βραχὺ γάρ που πάντως παρὰ τοῦ τὸ ἔλαττον εἰληφότος. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν τὸ χρῆμα ἐν νόμῳ γραφόμενον, καὶ ἀναλόγως τοῖς ἑκάστου μέτροις, τὰ παρ' αὐτοῦ ζητοῦντα Θεόν. Ἡμερότητος δὲ τῆς ἐπέκεινα λόγου καὶ φιλανθρωπίας ὑπάρχων πηγὴ καὶ γένεσις, ἀποπέμπεται μὲν οὐδένα τῶν διὰ πίστεως προσδεδραμηκότων αὐτῷ, προσίεται δὲ μεθ' ὧν ἂν ἕκαστος ἔχοι, καὶ δωροφορίας δέχεται πνευματικὰς, τὸ ἰσχύος ἐπέκεινα παραιτούμενος πανταχῆ. Ἔχει δὲ οὕτως ἡμῖν ὁ ἐπὶ τῷδε νόμος, ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Λάλησον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς αὐτοῖς· Ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἂν εὔξηται εὐχὴν ὥστε τιμὴν τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἔσται ἡ τιμὴ τοῦ ἄρσενος ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς ἕως ἑξηκονταετοῦς. ἔσται αὐτοῦ ἡ τιμὴ πεντήκοντα δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου τῷ σταθμῷ τῷ ἁγίῳ, τῆς δὲ θηλείας ἔσται ἡ συντίμησις τριάκοντα δίδραχμα. Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ πενταετοῦς ἕως εἴκοσι ἐτῶν, ἔσται ἡ τιμὴ τοῦ ἄρσενος εἴκοσι δίδραχμα, τῆς δὲ θηλείας, δέκα δίδραχμα. Ἀπὸ δὲ μηνιαίου ἕως πενταετοῦς, ἔσται ἡ τιμὴ τοῦ ἄρσενος πέντε δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου, τῆς δὲ θηλείας, τρία δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου. Ἐὰν δὲ ἀπὸ ἑξηκονταετῶν καὶ ἐπάνω, ἐὰν μὲν ἄρσεν ᾖ, ἔσται ἡ τιμὴ αὐτοῦ πέντε καὶ δέκα δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου· ἐὰν δὲ θήλεια, δέκα δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου· ἐὰν δὲ ταπεινὸς ᾖ τῇ τιμῇ, στήσεται ἐναντίον τοῦ ἱερέως, καὶ τιμήσεται αὐτὸν ὁ ἱερεὺς καθάπερ ἰσχύει ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ εὐξαμένου, οὕτως τιμήσεται αὐτὸν ὁ ἱερεύς.» Προσίεσαν μὲν γάρ τινες, ἑαυτοὺς εἰς ἁγιασμὸν καὶ ἀνάθημα καταγράφοντες τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ ἀνατιθέντες ἀσμένως τὴν τῷ νόμῳ διωρισμένην τῶν διδράχμων ποσότητα. Εἰ δὲ δή τις εἴη τῶν οὐ λίαν εὐσθενῶν, ἤγουν τῶν ἀσημοτέρων, οὐκέτι μὲν κατὰ νόμους ἡ ἔκτισις ἦν. Δοκιμάζοντος δὲ τοῦ κατὰ καιροὺς ἱερατεύοντος, ὄφλημά τι τοῖς αὐτοῦ μέτροις τὸ ἰσοπαλὲς ὡρίζετο. Αὕτη μὲν οὖν ἡ ἐμφανεστέρα τοῦ γράμματος ἀφήγησις καὶ ἔννοια· ἀναμνῆσαι δὲ δεῖν ἀναγκαῖον ὑπολαμβάνω τοὺς τοῖς ἱεροῖς προσεδρεύοντας λόγοις ὅτι μάλιστα φιλομαθῶς, ὡς τοῖς Φαρισαίοις ποτὲ προσελάλει Χριστὸς, καὶ ταυτησὶ σαφῶς τε καὶ ἐναργῶς διεμέμνητο τῆς ἐντολῆς. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ, εἰς ἐξίτηλόν τινα καὶ οὐχὶ τῷ νόμῳ διεγνωσμένον μεθορμισάμενοι βίον, καὶ διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, προσίεσαν λέγοντες, «Διατί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσι τὴν ἐντολὴν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων; Οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας, ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίουσι.» Παραχρῆμα δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ Σωτήρ· «Διατί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ; Ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς εἶπε, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, ἵνα εὖ σοι γένηται· ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε, Ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς, οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν μητέρα· καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν
pass_a_gloss: PALL. So I say myself; for so Christ said: 'to whom they entrusted (παρατίθημι) much, much they will seek (ζητέω) from him.' Clear that the reverse (τὸ ἔμπαλιν) is true too: little (βραχύ) surely from the one who received (λαμβάνω) the less (ἔλαττον). CYR. Behold (ἀθρέω) then the matter written in law, and God seeking the things from him proportionally to the measures of each. Being spring (πηγή) and origin (γένεσις) of gentleness (ἡμερότης) beyond word and of love for humankind (φιλανθρωπία), he sends away (ἀποπέμπω) none of those who have run toward (προστρέχω) him through faith (πίστις); he admits (προσίεμαι) [each] with whatever he has, and receives spiritual gift-bringings (δωροφορία πνευματική), everywhere (πανταχῆ) declining/excusing (παραιτέομαι) what is beyond strength (ἰσχύς). The law on this in Leviticus: [LXX Lev 27:1–8] 'A man who vows a vow (εὔχομαι εὐχήν) as a price (τιμή) of his soul (ψυχή) to the Lord: the price of the male (ἄρσην) from twenty years to sixty, his price fifty didrachms (δίδραχμον) of silver by the holy weight (σταθμὸς ἅγιος); of the female (θήλεια) the valuation (συντίμησις) thirty didrachms. From five to twenty: male twenty, female ten. From a month (μηνιαῖος) to five years: male five didrachms of silver, female three. From sixty and above: male fifteen, female ten. If he is low (ταπεινός) in the price, he shall stand before the priest (ἱερεύς), and the priest shall value (τιμάω) him as the hand of the one who vowed is able (ἰσχύει ἡ χείρ); so the priest shall value him.' For some approached, enrolling (καταγράφω) themselves into sanctification (ἁγιασμός) and dedication (ἀνάθημα) to God, and gladly (ἀσμένως) dedicating (ἀνατίθημι) the quantity of didrachms defined (διορίζω) by the law. If someone were of those not very strong (εὐσθενής), that is, of the more obscure (ἀσημότερος), the payment (ἔκτισις) was no longer according to laws; the one serving as priest at the time (κατὰ καιρούς) testing (δοκιμάζω), a debt (ὄφλημα) equal (ἰσοπαλής) to his measures was fixed (ὁρίζω). This then the plainer (ἐμφανεστέρα) narration (ἀφήγησις) and sense (ἔννοια) of the letter (γράμμα). I suppose it necessary to remind those attending (προσεδρεύω) the sacred words most studiously (φιλομαθῶς) that Christ once addressing the Pharisees clearly and vividly recalled (διαμέμνημαι) this commandment (ἐντολή). For they, having shifted anchorage (μεθορμίζομαι) into a fading/degenerate (ἐξίτηλος) life not discerned (διαγιγνώσκω) by the law, and teaching as teachings (διδασκαλία) commands (ἔνταλμα) of men, as written, approached saying: 'why do your disciples transgress (παραβαίνω) the commandment of the elders (πρεσβύτεροι)? for they do not wash (νίπτω) the hands when they eat bread.' At once the Savior (Σωτήρ): 'why do you also transgress the commandment of God? For God said: honor (τιμάω) your father and mother, that it may be well (εὖ) with you; but you say: whoever says to his father and mother, "a gift (δῶρον), whatever you might be benefited (ὠφελέω) from me," shall by no means honor (οὐ μὴ τιμήσει) his father and mother; and you annulled (ἀκυρόω) the commandment of God because of (διὰ τὴν) [continues §14: your tradition].'
pass_b_english: Palladius: I say so myself. For Christ said this: ‘From the one to whom they have entrusted much, they will ask much’ (Luke 12:48). And clearly the reverse is also true: surely little will be asked of the one who has received less.

Cyril: Look, then, at the matter as it is written in the law, and see God asking of each in proportion to each one’s measure. Being the spring and source of a gentleness and love for humankind beyond words, he sends away none of those who have run to him through faith; he welcomes each with whatever he has, and accepts spiritual offerings, in every case excusing what lies beyond a person’s strength. The law on this point reads as follows in Leviticus: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If anyone makes a vow to give the Lord the value of his own life, the valuation of a male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be this: his valuation shall be fifty didrachms of silver by the holy weight; and for a female the valuation shall be thirty didrachms. If from five years old to twenty years, the valuation of a male shall be twenty didrachms, and of a female ten didrachms. From one month old to five years old, the valuation of a male shall be five didrachms of silver, and of a female three didrachms of silver. And from sixty years old and upward, if it is a male, his valuation shall be fifteen didrachms of silver, and if a female, ten didrachms of silver. But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to what the hand of the one who vowed can afford, so the priest shall value him’ (Leviticus 27:1–8). For some came forward, enrolling themselves with God for consecration and as an offering dedicated to him, and gladly dedicating the sum of didrachms the law had fixed. But if someone was not very well off, that is, one of the humbler sort, the payment was no longer made by the legal scale; instead the priest serving at the time assessed him, and a debt matched to his means was set. This, then, is the plainer account and sense of the letter. But I think it necessary to remind those who attend to the sacred words with the greatest love of learning that Christ, speaking once to the Pharisees, called this very commandment to mind clearly and plainly. For they had turned aside into a debased way of life, one the law did not recognize, and were ‘teaching as doctrines the commandments of men,’ as it is written (Matthew 15:9; Isaiah 29:13), and they came to him saying: ‘Why do your disciples transgress the commandment of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread’ (Matthew 15:2). At once the Savior said to them: ‘Why do you also transgress the commandment of God? For God said, Honor your father and your mother, that it may be well with you (Exodus 20:12). But you say, Whoever says to his father and his mother, “Whatever help you might have had from me is a gift,” shall not honor his father and his mother. And you have made void the commandment of God for the sake of…’ (Matthew 15:3–6)

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

Luke 12:48 is quoted loosely (Cyril has ζητήσουσι παρ' αὐτοῦ where Luke has περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν in the second half). Leviticus 27:1–8 is LXX, where 'shekel' is rendered δίδραχμον ('didrachm'); kept as 'didrachms'. τιμὴ τῆς ψυχῆς rendered 'the value of his own life' (ψυχή = the person vowed). 'Teaching as doctrines the commandments of men' follows the word order of Matthew 15:9 (= Mark 7:7), which quotes LXX Isaiah 29:13; both cited. Matthew 15:2 is quoted with 'commandment of the elders' where Matthew has 'tradition of the elders', and Cyril's Matthew 15:3 lacks 'because of your tradition'; translated as Cyril gives them. 'That it may be well with you' is not in Matthew 15:4; Cyril adds it from LXX Exodus 20:12 (also Deuteronomy 5:16), hence the Exodus citation. οὐ μὴ τιμήσει (emphatic future negative) kept as 'shall not honor'; in Matthew it means the vow frees the son from honoring his parents. The section ends mid-phrase 'διὰ τὴν | παράδοσιν ὑμῶν' ('for the sake of | your tradition'); 'your tradition' falls at the head of §14. Possible but uncited echoes: 'He sends away none who have run to him' (John 6:37); 'spiritual gifts' (1 Peter 2:5, spiritual sacrifices).
